To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the weight-centric, non- weight-centric (health-centric) and health at every sizes approaches to weight bias have similarities and differences regarding the language used to describe people with large bodies; their theoretical positions; their identified influences on weight bias; and their identified consequences of weight-bias.

the three perspectives on weight bias are different in terms of their language and their theoretical orientation but share common ground in terms of their recognition of the negative consequences of this bias and their identification of the factors influencing it.
